column1: # boru Language Specification: KEYWORD SLOTS in fn signatures
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# A /q param whose atom names NO type is a KEYWORD slot: it matches
# exactly that one literal word (binding-agnostically, like every /q
# slot). This is the boru-source spelling of the keyword slots the def
# constructor forms use internally (`def name fn […]` matches the
# literal word `fn`) — the syntax-rules-literal mechanism, usable for
# user binder / DSL keywords. The kernel branch is patternsOk
# (eng/go/match.go); the parse is keywordParam (eng/go/fn_params.go).
# See design/STRICT-FORWARD-BARRIER.0.md.
# §1  an unnamed keyword slot matches ONLY its literal word
def betwixt fn [[a:Integer in/q b:Integer] [Integer] [b sub a]]  betwixt 3 in 10
column3: `in/q` admits the literal word `in`; a=3, b=10 → 10-3

column1: def betwixt fn [[a:Integer in/q b:Integer] [Integer] [b sub a]]  betwixt 3 to 10
column3: a different word (`to`) does not match the `in` keyword slot

column1: # §2  a keyword slot is BINDING-AGNOSTIC — a value bound to the keyword
#     name is irrelevant; the slot still matches only the literal word.
def in 99  def betwixt fn [[a:Integer in/q b:Integer] [Integer] [b sub a]]  betwixt 3 in 10
column3: `in` is bound to 99, but the keyword slot captures the literal word, not the binding

column1: # §3  a named keyword slot binds the captured atom to its name
def kw fn [[k:in/q] [Atom] [k]]  kw in
column3: `k:in/q` matches `in` and binds k to the atom `in` (renders in canonical /q form)

column1: def kw fn [[k:in/q] [Atom] [k]]  kw out
# §4  keyword slots compose with ordinary typed params and overloads
def q fn [[from/q n:Integer] [Integer] [n]  [to/q n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 10]]  q from 5
column3: the `from` keyword selects the first overload

column1: def q fn [[from/q n:Integer] [Integer] [n]  [to/q n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 10]]  q to 5
column3: the `to` keyword selects the second overload

column1: # §5  a capture-ANY /q slot (Atom/q, where Atom IS a type) is unchanged —
#     it captures any word, NOT a fixed literal.
def anyword fn [[w:Atom/q] [Atom] [w]]  anyword anything
column3: `Atom/q` still captures any bare word as its atom (canonical /q render)

column1: def anyword fn [[w:Atom/q] [Atom] [w]]  anyword other
# §6  a keyword-slot fn whose name collides with a CORE word is an
#     ownership compile failure (design/OPEN-WORDS.1.md): unanchored sigs can
#     no longer merge onto builtin words — pick a fresh name.
def between fn [[a:Integer in/q b:Integer] [Integer] [b sub a]]  between 3 in 10
column3: `between` is a core query word; the unanchored merge declines
